title: Control plane
description: Health of the kubeadm control plane of k8s01: kube-apiserver (availability SLO, errors, latency, load), etcd (leader, database size, disk latency), kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, kube-proxy and the certificates Prometheus can see. Formulas from the kubernetes-mixin and etcd mixin recording/alerting rules loaded here; curated companion of the official kps dashboards Kubernetes / API server, etcd, Scheduler, Controller Manager, Proxy.

list.name: etcd leader change
list.textFormat: single member: a leader change means etcd restarted

options.content:
**What this is.** The Kubernetes "brain" of k8s01, run by kubeadm as static pods in `kube-system`: **kube-apiserver**
(the only door to the cluster; Argo CD, kubectl, every controller talks to it), **etcd** (the database behind it, one member),
**kube-scheduler** (places pods), **kube-controller-manager** (Deployments, Jobs, node lifecycle, ...), **kube-proxy**
(Service iptables rules). It is a single node, so there is no redundancy: if one of these stops, the cluster stops changing
(running pods keep running).

**Healthy looks like:** top row all UP/green; API availability above 99 % (the kubernetes-mixin SLO) and error budget left;
no 5xx; read/write p99 latency well under 1 s; etcd has a leader, WAL fsync p99 below ~10 ms, database far from its quota;
no pending pods in the scheduler; kube-proxy applies rule changes within seconds; certificates months away from expiry.

**When something is red:**
- *A component DOWN* - `kubectl --context k8s01 -n kube-system get pods`, then the static pod logs on the node
  (`crictl logs`, manifests in /etc/kubernetes/manifests). Host-side changes belong to the Ansible repo (homelab-ansible).
- *API errors/latency* - usually etcd or the disk (etcd fsync, Disk I/O in *Cluster health*), or a misbehaving client
  (see APF and the "Objects stored" panel). Aggregated API down = metrics-server or KEDA (see *Cluster add-ons*).
- *etcd fsync/commit slow* - the SSD is saturated or failing: etcd needs low-latency disk ([etcd hardware guide](https://etcd.io/docs/v3.6/op-guide/hardware/)).
- *Certificate expiry close* - kubelet certs rotate automatically (approved by kubelet-csr-approver); kubeadm control-plane
  certificates are **not visible to Prometheus**: check them with `kubeadm certs check-expiration` on the node (they renew on
  every `kubeadm upgrade`).

**Expected empty/flat here:** 5xx and terminated requests (none), APF rejections (none), etcd peer traffic (single member,
not shown), scheduler `scheduler_volume_scheduling_*` (removed upstream, not shown).
Annotations: control-plane alerts (red), kube-system container restarts (orange), etcd leader changes (purple).

panels.title: Active alerts for this service
panels.description: Prometheus alerts of this service that are FIRING (condition true for longer than the rule's `for`) or PENDING (condition true, waiting for `for`). Same filter as the red alert annotations of this dashboard; Watchdog/InfoInhibitor are excluded. Empty = healthy. Alertmanager has no receiver in this lab, so dashboards are where alerts are seen: the rule, its threshold and source are in the rule files (helm-charts/<app>/**/prometheus.rules.yaml or the -raw release) and in docs/dashboards/. All alerts of the lab: dashboard "Alerts overview" (Observability folder).

panels.title: API server
panels.description: Prometheus can scrape kube-apiserver (KubeAPIDown fires when the target is absent, https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/alerts/system_alerts.libsonnet).

panels.title: API availability (30d)
panels.description:
Share of API requests over 30 days that were neither 5xx nor slower than the SLO
latency (1 s for resource-scoped reads and all writes, 5 s namespace-scoped, 30 s cluster-scoped). Recording rule
`apiserver_request:availability30d{verb="all"}` from kubernetes-mixin (https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/rules/kube_apiserver-availability.libsonnet).
Red below the mixin SLO of 99 %.

panels.title: Error budget left (30d)
panels.description:
How much of the 1 % monthly error budget (SLO 99 %) is still unused:
(availability30d - 0.99) / 0.01. Same quantity as the "ErrorBudget (30d)" panel of the kubernetes-mixin API server
dashboard (https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/dashboards/apiserver.libsonnet), expressed as a share of the budget. Below 0 = SLO violated.

panels.title: etcd
panels.description: Prometheus can scrape etcd metrics (http://<node>:2381, see helm-charts/monitoring kps values).

panels.title: etcd leader
panels.description:
Whether etcd has a leader (`etcd_server_has_leader`). Without a leader etcd refuses writes and
the API server fails. Source: etcd mixin alert etcdNoLeader (https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/tree/main/contrib/mixin).

panels.title: Scheduler
panels.description: kube-scheduler scraped (https :10259). KubeSchedulerDown when absent.

panels.title: Controller manager
panels.description: kube-controller-manager scraped (https :10257). KubeControllerManagerDown when absent.

panels.title: kube-proxy
panels.description: kube-proxy scraped (http :10249). KubeProxyDown when absent.

panels.title: Requests by status code
panels.description:
API requests per second by HTTP code, from recording rule
`code_resource:apiserver_request_total:rate5m` (kubernetes-mixin). 2xx dominate; 4xx are client mistakes (404 on
optional resources, 409 conflicts on updates are normal); 5xx are server failures and burn the error budget.

panels.title: 5xx error ratio
panels.description:
Share of read and write requests answered with 5xx, as in the "Read/Write SLI - Errors" panels
of the kubernetes-mixin API server dashboard (https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/dashboards/apiserver.libsonnet), from `code_resource:apiserver_request_total:rate5m`.
0 is normal here; the dashed line is the 1 % SLO budget.

targets.expr: (sum by (verb) (code_resource:apiserver_request_total:rate5m{code=~"5.."}) or 0 * sum by (verb) (code_resource:apiserver_request_total:rate5m)) / sum by (verb) (code_resource:apiserver_request_total:rate5m)

panels.title: Request latency p99 (worst resource)
panels.description:
99th percentile API latency for reads and writes, worst resource,
from recording rule `cluster_quantile:apiserver_request_sli_duration_seconds:histogram_quantile` (kubernetes-mixin
https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/rules/kube_apiserver-histogram.libsonnet; excludes long-running watch/exec/logs). The SLO counts a resource-scoped
read or any write slower than 1 s as an error (dashed line).

panels.title: Error-budget burn rate
panels.description:
How fast the API is consuming its error budget: bad events / all events over 1 h and
6 h (recording rules `apiserver_request:burnrate1h` / `burnrate6h`, kubernetes-mixin
https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/rules/kube_apiserver-burnrate.libsonnet). The multi-window alert KubeAPIErrorBudgetBurn fires (critical) above
14.4 % (1 h, with 5 m) and 6 % (6 h, with 30 m); 1 % = burning exactly the budget.

panels.title: In-flight and queued requests (APF)
panels.description:
Requests being executed right now by kind (`apiserver_current_inflight_requests`)
and requests waiting in API Priority and Fairness queues by priority level (`apiserver_flowcontrol_current_inqueue_requests`,
see https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/cluster-administration/flow-control/ and https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/instrumentation/metrics/). Queues should be ~0; a growing queue at one priority level means a noisy client.

panels.title: APF rejected (1h)
panels.description:
Requests rejected by API Priority and Fairness in the last hour
(`apiserver_flowcontrol_rejected_requests_total`, https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/cluster-administration/flow-control/): the client got HTTP 429. The counter only exists after the first
rejection, so 0 is shown when absent.

panels.title: Terminated requests
panels.description:
Share of requests the API server terminated (self-defence: timeouts, APF) over 10 min.
Formula of kubernetes-mixin alert KubeAPITerminatedRequests, red at 20 % (https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/alerts/system_alerts.libsonnet).

panels.title: Aggregated APIs unavailable
panels.description:
Number of aggregated APIServices the API server currently sees as unavailable
(`aggregator_unavailable_apiservice`): here v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io (metrics-server) and the KEDA external metrics API.
When one is down, `kubectl top`, HPAs/KEDA and API discovery (Argo CD!) can fail. Alert KubeAggregatedAPIDown
(https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/alerts/system_alerts.libsonnet).

panels.title: API server -> etcd latency p99
panels.description:
99th percentile duration of the API server's calls to etcd per operation (top 5),
`etcd_request_duration_seconds` (https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/instrumentation/metrics/). This is etcd latency as the API server feels it; when API latency rises,
look here first, then at etcd fsync below.

panels.title: Aggregated API errors
panels.description:
Times per interval the API server marked an aggregated APIService unavailable, by name and
reason (`aggregator_unavailable_apiservice_total`). Formula of alert KubeAggregatedAPIErrors
(https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/alerts/system_alerts.libsonnet). Flat 0 is healthy.

panels.title: Objects stored (top 10)
panels.description:
Number of objects per resource type stored in etcd (`apiserver_resource_objects`,
https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/instrumentation/metrics/). A type growing without bound (events, policy reports, ReplicaSets, Argo CD Applications history) inflates
etcd and slows LISTs.

panels.title: DB size
panels.description: Physical size of the etcd database file (`etcd_mvcc_db_total_size_in_bytes`, https://etcd.io/docs/v3.6/metrics/).

panels.title: DB vs quota
panels.description:
Database size / backend quota (`etcd_server_quota_backend_bytes`, 2 GiB by default). At 100 %
etcd raises the NOSPACE alarm and becomes read-only: the API server rejects all writes. Red at 95 % = etcd mixin alert
etcdDatabaseQuotaLowSpace (https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/tree/main/contrib/mixin).

panels.title: DB in use
panels.description:
Logical data / physical file size (`etcd_mvcc_db_total_size_in_use_in_bytes /
etcd_mvcc_db_total_size_in_bytes`). Low = fragmentation after compaction; space returns only after `etcdctl defrag`.
The etcd mixin alert etcdDatabaseHighFragmentationRatio fires below 50 % only when more than 100 MB are in use, so a low
value on a small database is harmless (no colour for that reason).

panels.title: Leader changes (24h)
panels.description:
Leader changes seen in 24 h (`etcd_server_leader_changes_seen_total`). With a single member
a change only happens when etcd restarts. The etcd mixin alert etcdHighNumberOfLeaderChanges fires at 4 in 15 min.

panels.title: Failed proposals (1h)
panels.description:
Raft proposals that failed in the last hour (`etcd_server_proposals_failed_total`,
https://etcd.io/docs/v3.6/metrics/): writes etcd could not commit. Should be 0 (alert etcdHighNumberOfFailedProposals, https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/tree/main/contrib/mixin).

panels.title: etcd memory
panels.description: Resident memory of the etcd process (process_resident_memory_bytes). Grows with DB size and watch count.

panels.title: Disk latency: WAL fsync and backend commit p99
panels.description:
99th percentile WAL fsync and backend commit durations, the
formulas of etcd mixin alerts etcdHighFsyncDurations (warning 0.5 s, critical 1 s) and etcdHighCommitDurations
(warning 0.25 s) (https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/tree/main/contrib/mixin). etcd's own guidance: p99 fsync under 10 ms on a good SSD (https://etcd.io/docs/v3.6/op-guide/hardware/). Slow fsync = slow
API writes and, at worst, a leader that cannot heartbeat.

panels.title: Database size vs quota
panels.description:
Physical DB size, logical in-use size and the backend quota (dashed). The gap between
total and in-use is reclaimable by defragmentation. Growth projected past the quota within 4 h fires
etcdExcessiveDatabaseGrowth (https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/tree/main/contrib/mixin).

panels.title: Raft proposals and gRPC failures
panels.description:
Committed proposals per second (write load), pending proposals (should stay near
0; growing = etcd cannot keep up) and the share of failed gRPC requests (formula of etcd mixin alert
etcdHighNumberOfFailedGRPCRequests: warning 1 %, critical 5 %, right axis) (https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/tree/main/contrib/mixin).

panels.title: etcd gRPC request latency p99 (unary, by method)
panels.description: 99th percentile time etcd takes to answer each gRPC method the API server calls (Range = reads, Txn = writes, LeaseGrant = leases for Events/leader election). Needs etcd `--metrics=extensive` (enabled through homelab-ansible on 2026-11-15). Formula and thresholds from the etcd mixin alert etcdGRPCRequestsSlow (https://github.com/etcd-io/etcd/blob/main/contrib/mixin/mixin.libsonnet): p99 > 0.15 s for 10 min = warning, > 1 s = critical; Defragment excluded (always slow by design). On a single node this is dominated by disk fsync latency: compare with the WAL fsync panel; sustained red means the node disk is too slow for etcd.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (grpc_service, grpc_method, le) (rate(grpc_server_handling_seconds_bucket{job="kube-etcd", grpc_type="unary", grpc_method!="Defragment"}[$__rate_interval]))) > 0

panels.title: Scheduler leader
panels.description:
Whether this kube-scheduler holds the leader lease (`leader_election_master_status`). With one
instance it must be 1; 0 means it lost the lease (API server unreachable) and nothing is being scheduled.

panels.title: Controller-manager leader
panels.description:
Same for kube-controller-manager: 0 = no controller is reconciling (Deployments,
Jobs, garbage collection, node lifecycle stop).

panels.title: Unschedulable pods
panels.description:
Pods the scheduler could not place, summed over the plugins that rejected them
(`scheduler_unschedulable_pods`, https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/instrumentation/metrics/). Typical causes on one node: Insufficient cpu/memory requests,
unbound PVC, taints, nvidia.com/gpu already taken.

panels.title: Scheduling p99
panels.description:
99th percentile end-to-end pod scheduling latency (from the pod entering the queue to being bound),
recording rule `cluster_quantile:scheduler_pod_scheduling_sli_duration_seconds:histogram_quantile` (kubernetes-mixin
https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/rules/kube_scheduler.libsonnet). Milliseconds normally; NaN/no value when nothing was scheduled recently.

panels.title: Control-plane API client 5xx
panels.description:
5xx responses per second received by the control-plane components and kubelet
when calling the API server (`rest_client_requests_total{code=~"5.."}`), the "Kube API Request Rate" 5xx series of the
kps Scheduler/Controller Manager/Kubelet/Proxy dashboards (https://github.com/prometheus-community/helm-charts/tree/kube-prometheus-stack-93.3.0/charts/kube-prometheus-stack/templates/grafana/dashboards-1.14). 0 when absent.

panels.title: Scheduler attempts with error (1h)
panels.description:
Scheduling attempts that ended in an internal error in the last hour
(`scheduler_schedule_attempts_total{result="error"}`, https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/instrumentation/metrics/). Unschedulable is not an error; this is.

panels.title: Scheduler queue
panels.description:
Pods waiting in the scheduler queues (`scheduler_pending_pods` by queue, https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/instrumentation/metrics/): active
(being tried), backoff (failed recently), unschedulable (waiting for a cluster change), gated (scheduling gates).
Should be 0 most of the time.

panels.title: Scheduling attempts by result
panels.description:
Scheduling attempts per second by result (scheduled / unschedulable / error),
`scheduler_schedule_attempts_total` (https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/instrumentation/metrics/).

panels.title: Controller-manager work queues (top 10 depth)
panels.description:
Items waiting in the controller-manager work queues
(`workqueue_depth`, as in "Work Queue Depth" of Kubernetes / Controller Manager, https://github.com/prometheus-community/helm-charts/tree/kube-prometheus-stack-93.3.0/charts/kube-prometheus-stack/templates/grafana/dashboards-1.14/controller-manager.yaml).
Spikes during rollouts are normal; a queue that stays high means a controller is stuck or throttled by the API server.

panels.title: Rule changes not applied
panels.description:
Seconds a Service/Endpoint change has been waiting to be written to iptables (IPv4):
last queued time minus last sync time, clamped at 0 (`kubeproxy_sync_proxy_rules_last_queued_timestamp_seconds`,
`kubeproxy_sync_proxy_rules_last_timestamp_seconds`, https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/instrumentation/metrics/). kube-proxy's /healthz turns unhealthy with the same
comparison after 2x syncPeriod (60 s by default): red. IPv6 is ignored (not used here, it syncs only hourly).

panels.title: Rules sync and network programming p99
panels.description:
99th percentile time to write iptables rules
(`kubeproxy_sync_proxy_rules_duration_seconds`) and end-to-end network programming latency, i.e. from an Endpoint change in
the API to the rule being active (`kubeproxy_network_programming_duration_seconds`). Same quantiles as the kps Proxy
dashboard (https://github.com/prometheus-community/helm-charts/tree/kube-prometheus-stack-93.3.0/charts/kube-prometheus-stack/templates/grafana/dashboards-1.14/proxy.yaml). Seconds-long values mean new pods receive Service traffic late.

panels.title: iptables rules
panels.description:
Number of iptables rules kube-proxy manages per table (`kubeproxy_sync_proxy_rules_iptables_total`,
https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/instrumentation/metrics/). Grows with Services x endpoints; a jump shows a new app or a Service with many ports.

panels.title: Kubelet serving cert
panels.description:
Time left on the kubelet's serving certificate (`kubelet_certificate_manager_server_ttl_seconds`).
It is issued by the cluster CA through a CSR that kubelet-csr-approver approves (serverTLSBootstrap); metrics-server and
Prometheus verify it. Thresholds = kubernetes-mixin alerts KubeletServerCertificateExpiration (warning 7 d, critical 1 d,
https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/alerts/kubelet.libsonnet). The kubelet renews at ~70-90 % of the lifetime.

panels.title: Kubelet client cert
panels.description:
Time left on the kubelet's client certificate used to talk to the API server
(`kubelet_certificate_manager_client_ttl_seconds`), auto-rotated. Thresholds = KubeletClientCertificateExpiration
(7 d / 1 d).

panels.title: Shortest client cert seen by API
panels.description:
1st percentile of the remaining lifetime of client certificates presented to the
API server (`apiserver_client_certificate_expiration_seconds`), formula of KubeClientCertificateExpiration (warning 7 d,
critical 1 d, https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/alerts/system_alerts.libsonnet), here over 1 h instead of 5 m so it does not go blank between requests.
The histogram's last bucket is 1 year: "1 year" means "at least a year". Covers kubelet, scheduler, controller-manager,
admin kubeconfig clients.

panels.title: Kubelet cert renewal errors (24h)
panels.description:
Failed kubelet certificate renewals in 24 h (`kubelet_server_expiration_renew_errors`
+ `kubelet_certificate_manager_client_expiration_renew_errors`), the counters behind KubeletServer/ClientCertificateRenewalErrors
(https://github.com/kubernetes-monitoring/kubernetes-mixin/tree/master/alerts/kubelet.libsonnet). Server-cert errors usually mean the CSR was not approved: check kubelet-csr-approver.

panels.title: CPU by kube-system pod
panels.description:
CPU cores used by each kube-system pod (control plane, CoreDNS, kube-proxy,
metrics-server, kubelet-csr-approver), recording rule `node_namespace_pod_container:container_cpu_usage_seconds_total:sum_rate5m`
(kubernetes-mixin). The API server and etcd should dominate; a sudden jump usually follows a client flooding the API.

panels.title: Memory by kube-system pod (working set)
panels.description:
Working-set memory of each kube-system pod, recording rule
`node_namespace_pod_container:container_memory_working_set_bytes` (kubernetes-mixin). The API server caches every object
it watches: its memory grows with the number of objects (see "Objects stored").
